title: FAMILY: Tick, Tick, Tick
author: Michael Foster
summary: Michael Foster warns that wasting time is a slow, invisible illness because it rarely feels dangerous while it is happening. Distracted attention masquerades as vigilance, responsibility, or staying informed. Young men in particular spend time freely because it feels endless, assuming there will always be more time to become the husband, father, or man they intend to be. But the consequences accumulate: the inattentive father whose grown son no longer thinks to call, the wife who stopped trying to connect, the discipline that never formed. Repentance and forgiveness are possible, but they do not always remove earthly consequences of wasted years. The most important work most men will ever do is not flashy -- it is the ordinary faithfulness of listening, praying, teaching, working, and being fully present with the people God gave them to love. That kind of faithful life is built slowly, day by day; and so is its opposite.
points: Wasted time is dangerous precisely because it feels harmless in the moment -- small, justified, easily explained.
The earthly consequences of chronically wasted years are not always reversible even after genuine repentance and forgiveness.
Distracted fathers model distraction for their children -- the pattern they establish is what gets inherited.
The most important male work is unglamorous: daily faithfulness in listening, teaching, praying, and being present.
Ordinary faithfulness is built slowly across days; so is its neglect -- neither happens suddenly or all at once.
quotes: Wasting time is costly because it rarely feels dangerous while it is happening.
The child you were too distracted to notice becomes the grown son who no longer thinks to call when he is in town.
You can repent. You can change. You can be forgiven. But forgiveness does not always remove the earthly consequences of wasted years.

The most important work most men will ever do is not flashy. It is the ordinary work of daily faithfulness. Listening well. Praying consistently. Teaching patiently. Working hard. Paying attention. Being fully present where God has placed you.
What a tragedy to become deeply informed about things far away while neglecting the people sitting across from you in your own living room.
